steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic; cook and stir until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, breaking up with a fork. Stir in basil, salt, and pepper; simmer for 15 minutes. Stir in vodka and cook 15 minutes more.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes; drain.
Stir cream into sauce; cook 10 minutes more. Toss with hot pasta.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta alla Vodka
raw_recipe.description: This pasta alla vodka recipe is easy to put together for a delicious dinner. The penne swimming in vodka-infused tomato sauce is simply irresistible!
raw_recipe.name: Pasta alla Vodka

review.reviewBody: Vodka sauces are wonderful and so easy to make! I sauteed some chopped onion in olive oil along with 3 cloves of garlic. I then added 1/4 tsp. of red pepper flakes. I used a 28 oz. can of crushed tomatoes instead of whole and then 2 tsp. of sugar to cut the acidity of the tomatoes. I also added a bit of parmesan cheese along with the cream and the sauce came out very smooth and oh so good over the penne pasta. Great with garlic bread!

One word...WOW...made this for a large Sunday family dinner. Used recipe for 18 servings, 3 pounds of pasta. Others commented that it was too much cream so I used half of what was called for. Simmered it about 15 minutes longer than directed. After draining the pasta, I poured the sauce into the pot, stirred it up, and let it sit covered about 10 minutes before serving. Everybody was extremely impressed. Will surely make this again.

Tasty recipe, I sautéed 1lb of shrimp and added it soon after the cream. Well actually I used a half pint of half and half. I suggest tempering the cream so it doesn't curdle. Put the cream in a bowl and add some of the heated sauce by the spoonful until it's warm.

I sauteed porcini mushrooms and zucchini first, then added a dash of red pepper flakes, along with Herbamare salt and oregano and a touch of garlic powder. Also browned sausage and added that at the end. A great meal that lasts for days. I have used half and half before and even creme fraiche--both great substitutes.

Great recipe; very easy. I doubled the recipe, but still only used 1 pint heavy cream... I added a little crushed red pepper... I added Beyond Meat Beef Crumbles at the very end of the cook time, just enough time for them to get to temperature. I am pretty sure the Titos Vodka is the secret 

it fed 8 people, with enough leftovers for a few lunches this week.

I made this today for the first time and I made a few changes. I used crushed tomatoes (28oz) instead of peeled and added a small can of diced tomatoes (14oz). I added about 1/4 tsp of crushed red pepper and used about 4 garlic cloves as opposed to two. I also used about half the amount of heavy cream. With these changes the sauce came out phenomenal! As it sits, the sauce does get a little thicker. Definitely making this again!

I gave this 3 stars because it is a good base recipe, but we found it bland. We like a meat sauce, so I browned 1 lb of ground Italian sausage. Then I mixed in 2, 14oz cans of crushed tomatoes. Then I followed the directions as is. I added some Parmesan cheese to the cream sauce too.

Simplicity and sophistication at its finest! Wow, the flavors were an ultimate in comfort food with a bit of restaurant fanciness. Pasta is a favorite for many and that includes picky me! Making this recipe with my personal twist has elevated my pasta game!! I personalized this recipe with the following: • Used Mostaccioli because it was in my pantry • Used San Marzano canned tomatoes because it’s my favorite • Used lemon pepper vs plain black pepper because it’s my favorite too • Finished the dish with sprinkles of red pepper flakes and Romano Cheese
SO good !!! I use crushed tomatoes as well as a small can of diced tomatoes. I also add sweet Italian sausages and 1 teaspoon of crushed red pepper! Phenomenal recipe!!!

Great recipe. One easy step to take to enhance it is to boil and shred some chicken and toss it with the pasta sauce at the very end. I also add a little bit of smoked paprika to make it sweeter, but that comes down to personal preference and I only discovered this effect because I accidentally mixed up my pepper and paprika, so YMMV.

My kids and I love this sauce! I did make two slight changes. I did a quick pulse blend to break up tomatoes before I added them to the pan. My kids didn't like the chunks. Also, I used only about a 1/4 cup of heavy cream. Way too creamy with original amount. Overall delicious!
Followed the recipe but I did add half of a small sweet onion with the garlic. S9 good. Best recipe ever. I will definitely make it again soon.
Delicious & easy. I added chopped onion sautéed along with the garlic.

I added grated parmesan and Tysons precooked chicken and OMG it is soooooo good. I don't even like this dish lol but made it foe my son in laws birthday because this is his favorite. I used 3/4 cup heavy cream and that seemed to be the right combination. Mmmmmmmmmm

This is a simpler version of penne alla vodka. It doesn't have anything extra. It's good if you have picky eaters. I prefer the frills and extras though, I think it adds interest and needed texture to the dish. Hence, 4 stars and not 5.

It was good. The "salt and pepper to taste" is a wide range, but that's OK. I used Ripple brand non dairy milk in deference to my daughter that has a dairy allergy. I also cooked some chicken in advance and tossed that in at the end. Would make again.
